body: CRITICAL CORRECTION / STRONGER BOUNDARY: `console.example.com` and `audience.example.com` are separate ORIGINS but the same SITE. `SameSite=Strict` cookies will still be sent on requests initiated by the sibling origin, and `Sec-Fetch-Site` will report `same-site`, not `cross-site`. Host-only `__Host-` cookies prevent the audience host from reading/setting the console cookie, but do not by themselves prevent sibling-origin CSRF. Therefore: (A) strongest recommendation is separate registrable domains (e.g. `presenter-app.example` and `audience-display.example`) plus no CORS; cross-site `SameSite=Strict` then becomes a real extra barrier; OR (B) if subdomains are operationally required, exact Origin allowlist + synchronizer CSRF token on every state change and exact Origin on WSS are non-negotiable—never accept merely `same-site`. The cross-origin Window Management/window.open/WSS lifecycle I sent remains the same across different sites. This also avoids broad Clear-Site-Data/cookie-domain interactions. Sources: OWASP CSRF and WebSocket sheets plus MDN cookie/Sec-Fetch-Site docs.
